referents.why: 'your' (2ms) is inside the speech Moses is to say to Aaron, so it is the addressee of that speech: Aaron's staff.
'Say to Aaron' is a command inside the LORD's speech to Moses; the implied 'you' is the one the LORD is speaking to, Moses. Aaron is the one Moses is to speak to, not the one commanded here.
referents.category: implied subject of a command that introduces a speech

referents.why: 'Stretch out your staff' belongs to the speech Moses is to say to Aaron, so the implied 'you' is Aaron; the 'your' of 'your staff' agrees.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: Same speech as the clause before; the waw joins the second command to the first, so the implied 'you' is still Aaron.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: 'It will become gnats': a third masculine singular weqatal whose subject is what the preceding command acted on, the dust (masculine singular); the staff was stretched out, not turned into gnats, and the act decides.
referents.category: implied subject is what the previous clause acted on

links.why: cl3 is a command inside a speech nested two deep; the narrative line of cl0 does not continue into it.
links.category: link from inside a speech to the narrative line

links.why: Two commands joined by a separate-word waw (וְ) at one level, 'stretch out ... and strike'.
A weqatal after an imperative says what the commands bring about, which is `result`, not a plain narrative sequence.
links.category: effect of a command read as plain sequence

links.why: Imperative, then waw + third-person weqatal 'and it will become gnats': what the commanded acts will bring about.
'The LORD said to Moses' and what he said: the command to say to Aaron, taken with its content.
links.category: speech clause and what was said

links.why: 'Say to Aaron' and what Moses is to say: the run of commands joined by 'and' at one level, taken as one imperative group.
links.category: speech clause and what was said (nested speech)

groups.why: The LORD speaks to Moses; what is said is the command to say something to Aaron, which is the nested turn, not cl1-cl4 flattened as direct parts.
groups.category: nested speech held as a part of the outer turn

groups.why: Moses is told to say to Aaron: the sender is the one commanded (the implied 'you' of cl1, Moses), the addressee Aaron, and what is said is the imperative group.
groups.category: nested speech, sender is the one commanded

groups.why: Commands joined by 'and' at one level are one imperative group with several command members; the waw + third-person weqatal after them is its effect.
groups.category: commands joined by and form one group with a shared effect

groups.why: Folded into imp2: cl3 is a second command of the same group, not a separate one with cl4 as its own effect; keeping both would count cl3 twice.
groups.category: one group split into two overlapping groups
